prompt: Write an email to a colleague about pests eating the vegetables. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: The vegetables, and who is eating them

Dear Colleague,

I write with news from the garden, and it is not the good kind. Something has been eating the vegetables; I have not yet established what, but I have my suspects, and I intend to question each of them in turn.

The first casualty was the lettuce. I had seen on Tuesday that it was just ready to cut, and I went out on Wednesday with a bowl and a certain amount of confidence. The bowl came back empty. The lettuce had been reduced to a sort of green lace, which is handsome in a curtain but of little use in a salad. The beans fared little better; their leaves are now so full of holes that they resemble a map of some archipelago.

The evidence so far points in two directions. There are slugs, certainly, for the silver trails across the path are as good as a signed confession. But slugs do not account for the squash, whose stems have been gnawed through at the base, a piece of work that requires either teeth or a grudge. I am inclined to blame a rabbit, though the neighbor insists it is a groundhog, and we have agreed to disagree with the cool formality of two nations disputing a border.

I have tried the usual remedies. A saucer of beer, set out for the slugs, was drained by morning; I counted this a partial success, as the slugs did at least die happy. I have also scattered crushed eggshells, which are said to discourage them. They have not been discouraged. If anything, they seem to regard the shells as a pleasant sort of gravel drive leading directly to the cabbages.

I am told that you had a similar trouble with your own plot a few seasons ago, and that you won the contest in the end. I would be grateful for the details of your method, whether it was netting, traps, a dog, or some arrangement I have not thought of. I am prepared to try nearly anything short of a formal treaty with the groundhog.

If you have an hour free this weekend, come and look at the damage yourself. I will provide the coffee, and you may provide the expert opinion; the vegetables, what is left of them, will provide the evidence.

With thanks in advance,

Walter
